draft.title: Profit
card: Revenue is the money a business earns from selling its goods or services. Expenses are the costs of running the business, such as wages, rent and stock.
Profit is revenue minus expenses. It is what is left over once every expense has been paid out of revenue.
Owners risk their own money when they start or invest in a business. Profit rewards them for taking that risk. Profit kept in the business can pay for growth, such as new equipment or a second shop.
When expenses are more than revenue, the result is a loss. A business cannot keep making losses for long, because it runs out of money.
draft.remember: Profit is what is left after expenses. It rewards the owners' risk and pays for growth.

a.q: A bakery in Ballarat has revenue of $120,000 and expenses of $135,000 for the year. What is the result?
a.why: Revenue minus expenses is $120,000 minus $135,000, which is negative $15,000. Expenses are more than revenue, so it is a loss, not a profit of $15,000.
a.clue: Which is bigger here, revenue or expenses?

b.q: Priya put $30,000 of her savings into a bike repair shop in Hobart. Why does she expect the shop to earn a profit?
opts: Profit rewards her for risking her savings
Profit is the same as the shop's revenue
Profit is needed to pay the shop's expenses
Profit is a payment the government makes to owners
b.why: Priya could lose her savings if the shop fails, and profit is her reward for taking that risk. Expenses are paid out of revenue first. Profit is what is left after that, so it does not pay the expenses.
b.clue: What could Priya lose by starting the shop?

b.best: Profit rewards her for risking her savings
